title: CAPIT Methodology | Sources, Verification, and Publication Rules
description: How CAPIT collects, normalizes, verifies, and publishes state well-plugging records, how tokens are minted on Base, and the limits of what CAPIT verifies.
headline: CAPIT Methodology
body: This page explains how CAPIT collects state source records, decides which records to publish, handles revisions, and links each published record to token activity on the Base network. It also sets out the limits of what CAPIT verifies.

sections.heading: How the Pipeline Works
sections.body: Every record moves through the same five stages: collection, normalization, verification, publication, and minting. A token is minted only for a record that has passed every earlier stage.

sections.heading: Data Collection & Source Hierarchy
sections.body: CAPIT prioritizes primary regulatory sources: state oil and gas agencies and state geological surveys. Records are retrieved from published data files, database exports, and GIS map services. Where a state offers none of these, CAPIT retrieves records from the agency's public web portal. Each record keeps its source agency, source system, and retrieval date.

sections.heading: Normalization & Deduplication
sections.body: State data fields vary widely. CAPIT maps incoming records into one schema, matches wells by API number (the standard U.S. well identifier), and uses location data to catch duplicates. Each state's original status term is kept alongside CAPIT's display label.

sections.heading: What CAPIT Verifies, and What It Doesn't
sections.body: CAPIT verifies that a plugged-status record exists at the source agency, that it is unique, and that it meets CAPIT's publication rules. CAPIT does not inspect wells in the field, measure emissions, or confirm surface restoration. Those remain the responsibility of operators and state regulators.

sections.heading: 1:1 Minting Logic
sections.body: Exactly one CAPIT token is minted on Base for each unique plugged-well record CAPIT publishes. Tokens are never minted without a matching published record, so supply grows only as records are added. The contract's minting roles and permissions are visible on the verified contract on BaseScan.

sections.heading: Revision Handling
sections.body: When a state agency updates, corrects, or reclassifies a well record, CAPIT adds a new revision instead of overwriting the old one. The full history stays visible on the record, so no change happens silently.

sections.heading: Known Limitations
sections.body: Keep these in mind when reading CAPIT figures:
bullets: Records can lag the source agency by days to months, depending on each state's update schedule.
CAPIT counts records it has published, not every well plugged nationally. Coverage differs by state.
Some older plugged wells have no plugging date in state databases.
Status definitions differ by state, so state totals are not always directly comparable.
